newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO to set date for enlargement summit.
newsitem.headline: NATO to set date for enlargement summit.

text.p: NATO foreign ministers will set a date later this week for a summit next year to invite former communist countries to join the alliance, but will try to assuage Russian fears by offering not to station nuclear weapons on the territory of any new members, diplomats said on Monday.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher told reporters NATO foreign ministers, meeting in Brussels on Tuesday and Wednesday, would fix a date for an "enlargement summit" and its agenda.
"The meeting tomorrow will be significant in setting a date for that NATO summit next year and a full agenda of decisions for that summit," he told reporters.
Diplomatic sources said the summit would be held in July in a European capital, probably Madrid, and the most likely current dates were July 7-9.

Some former satellites of the defunct Soviet Union in central and eastern Europe are clamouring to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) -- for years the West's defence bulwark against the Moscow-led Warsaw Pact.
Russia is resolutely opposed to plans to expand the alliance eastwards, warning it risks creating a new dividing line in Europe.

NATO foreign ministers, while insisting the enlargement timetable is non-negotiable, are expected to adopt a declaration stressing the alliance has no intention of moving nuclear weapons on to the territory of any new members.
Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are the three countries most likely to be asked to open membership talks, but Slovenia and Romania are also in the frame, diplomats say.

NATO Secretary General Javier Solana will also be authorised to open a formal dialogue with Russia over a new NATO-Russia charter governing all aspects of the relationship between the former Cold War foes.
